title: Effect of bradykinin receptor antagonism on ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema
authors: Straka BT, Ramirez CE, Byrd JB, Stone E, Woodard-Grice A, Nian H, et al.
journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
population: Patients with ACE-inhibitor-associated angio-oedema of lips, tongue, pharynx or face at Vanderbilt University Medical Center (2007 to 2015) and Massachusetts General Hospital (2012); two-thirds African American and two-thirds women
funder: This study was partially supported by UL1 RR024975 and R01HL079184 from the National Institutes of Health, and the Investigator-Initiated Research Program from Jerini AG/Shire Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Drs. Straka, Byrd, and Woodard-Grice were funded by T32GM007569.
authorConflicts: Brown is a consultant for Novartis, serves on the scientific advisory board of Alnylam, has consulted for Shire and received research funding from New Haven Pharmaceuticals and Shire.
result: 33 randomised and 31 treated (13 icatibant 30 mg at 0 and 6 hours, 18 placebo). Time to resolution of symptoms was similar (P=0.19 for the primary symptom), as was use of antihistamines, corticosteroids and adrenaline. The authors conclude that the study does not support clinical efficacy of a bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist in ACE-inhibitor-associated angio-oedema.
